newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's picks DDB Needham as lead US ad agency.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's picks DDB Needham as lead US ad agency.

text.p: Fast-food giant McDonald's Corp said Tuesday it chose DDB Needham, a unit of Omnicom Group Inc, as its lead advertising agency in the United States, responsible for all adult and promotion advertising activity.
DDB Needham, which takes over as lead agency from Leo Burnett Co, also will be responsible for McDonald's overall brand position and creative direction.

McDonald's said Leo Burnett will continue to work on its U.S. advertising account, developing its marketing strategies for its children's, "tween" and Ronald McDonald business. The "tween" market includes pre-teens and young teenagers.
Ball said no changes have been made to McDonald's regional and specialty advertising.
"We will be looking for an overall theme and brand positioning coming from DDB Needham," Ball said in an interview.
Advertising for McDonald's international business was not affected by this decision.
Ball said the decision regarding media-buying responsibilities for its adult and promotional business will be announced over the next 90 days.
DDB Needham's selection as lead agency becomes effective immediately, Ball said.
Both Burnett and DDB Needham made presentations to McDonald's last week, and a new campaign is scheduled to begin in September, advertising sources said.
Burnett had been the lead advertising agency for McDonald's since 1981. DDB Needham previously had the lead from 1970 to 1981.

McDonald's has a total advertising budget of about $600 million, which includes national, regional and specialty promotions targeted at Hispanic and African-American consumers. Of that, about $450 million is earmarked for general market advertising.

The competition for the account follows a misstep in what was expected to be a long term national promotion. This spring, McDonald's launched its Campaign 55, offering a hamburger for 55 cents when a customer also bought a drink and french fries. Some U.S. franchisees had complained that the promotion failed to build sales and hurt profit margins.
Most of Campaign 55 was abandoned after six weeks because it also failed to generate targeted lunch and dinner traffic.
McDonald's has more than 12,000 restaurants in the United States and nearly 22,000 worldwide.

Its domestic business has been under pressure from intensified competition in the U.S. fast-food market, particularly from rivals Burger King, a unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, and Wendy's International Inc.
In 1996, McDonald's share of the quick-service hamburger market slipped 0.2 percentage points to 42.1 percent, according to restaurant consultant Technomic.
McDonald's recently realigned its U.S. management, which it said would move decision-making closer to the restaurant and franchisee-level.
